Africa has made real progress on energy access over the past decade, with electrification in sub-Saharan Africa rising from around 51% in 2017 to over 61% in 2023. Yet nearly two out of every five people in Africa still lack electricity, as population growth continues to outpace connections. Progress is happening — but not yet at the speed or scale required.

The opportunity is immense. Africa holds 60% of the world’s best solar resources, more than 7,900 GW of solar potential, over 400 GW of hydropower, and vast wind and geothermal corridors. These resources position Africa to build clean, resilient energy systems that power development, jobs, and economic transformation.

As energy demand grows, the challenge is no longer only expanding access — but how to use data, digitalization, and AI to plan better, invest smarter, and deliver faster. Digital intelligence can help turn clean energy into a true platform for inclusion and growth.

This is why the Africa SDG 7 Report matters. It offers a data-driven picture of progress in most resent years and outlines what must change to stay on track for 2030.
